global_briefing: Trump's Asia trip, with reported deals in Manila and Shenzhen, will set the terms of Chinese licences for rare earths, antimony and tungsten. US curbs on China's remote access to AI chips and a China data-centre curb slow Chinese compute growth, relocating power and copper demand rather than cancelling it. Mongolia's president's resignation over alleged corruption adds policy risk to Oyu Tolgoi, which depends on China-facing exports. Gulf shipping risk feeds diesel, freight and sulphur costs at North American mines first. Japan and the Philippines' economic security pledge ties Asian mineral supply to security blocs.
